title: selective-fallback-policy-and-dynamic-precision-for-latency-sensitive-paths
author: Aisha Mendez
release_notes: Introduce selective fallback policy and a dynamic precision toggle to reduce tail latency for latency-sensitive routes. Backwards compatible; opt-in via config.
description:
Summary: Implement a selective fallback policy plus a dynamic precision toggle and scheduler heuristics that route only high-risk requests to conservative kernels while keeping the fast kernels for the common case. This reduces 99th percentile latency for interactive routes without broadly sacrificing throughput or eviction correctness.

Motivation: The existing fallback-on-every-error approach is too conservative for many interactive workloads. We observed that a small fraction of sequences trigger correctness guards and force slow kernels for all concurrent work on the same worker, causing tail latency amplification. This PR introduces heuristics that: 1) identify high-risk requests at admission time, 2) apply safe-mode kernels only to those requests, and 3) allow other requests to continue on fast paths with a dynamic precision toggle that can temporarily relax precision for short-lived tokens. The goal is to balance correctness guarantees for vulnerable inputs with overall latency and throughput improvements.

Design: - admission classifier: lightweight checks based on sequence length, token-entropy hints from tokenizer, and presence of structured output constraints. Tunable thresholds are stored in configs/fallback_policy.yaml. - request tagging: requests that fail conservative checks are tagged as safe_mode=true and routed to conservative kernels. Others are allowed to take fast kernels; if a downstream kernel returns an invalidation, only that request is elevated and its KV entries are quarantined to avoid polluting shared caches. - dynamic precision toggle: the kernel_selector can change precision (fp32->fp16/quantized) for non-critical tokens for a bounded prefix window; toggles are logged and decay after N tokens. - KV cache isolation: kv_cache_manager adds lightweight per-request quarantine buckets and probabilistic re-insertion after validation. - scheduler changes: admission is integrated into the continuous batcher so that mixed batches are split gracefully rather than forcing entire batch to safe-mode.

Implementation notes: commits touch runtime and rust components: - src/runtime/scheduler.cc: split batch paths and gating hooks added. - src/runtime/kernel_selector.cc: new precision_toggle API and telemetry. - services/kv/kv_cache_manager.rs: quarantine and reinsertion logic with eviction-safe guards. - configs/fallback_policy.yaml: default thresholds and tuning knobs. - tests/perf/fallback_latency_test.py: benchmark harness that runs synthetic and real prompts. - docs/design/fallback_isolation.md: design doc describing correctness properties and rollout guidance.

Commits: - Add selective fallback admission classifier and default config (Aisha) - 2026-02-18 - Add precision toggle API to kernel selector and unit tests (Aisha) - 2026-02-19 - Implement KV quarantine and reinsertion policy (Aisha) - 2026-02-20 - Integrate admission into continuous batcher, split mixed batches (Aisha) - 2026-02-21 - Add perf harness and perf benches, tune thresholds (Aisha) - 2026-02-23

Changed files summary: - src/runtime/scheduler.cc: add split_batch_for_safe_mode and metrics hooks - src/runtime/kernel_selector.cc/h: add set_dynamic_precision and query_precision_hint - services/kv/kv_cache_manager.rs: add quarantine buckets, probabilistic reinsertion - configs/fallback_policy.yaml: new default config - tests/perf/fallback_latency_test.py: new benchmark harness - docs/design/fallback_isolation.md: new design doc

Small snippet (admission classifier pseudocode):

if (seq_len > config.max_fast_seq) or (token_entropy > config.entropy_threshold) or (requires_strict_output) then
  tag request safe_mode=true
else
  tag request safe_mode=false
end

Testing and results: - Unit tests added for kernel_selector API and KV quarantine logic. - Perf run on staging cluster (p3.2xlarge equivalent) with rw-mix workload: baseline main branch 99p = 320ms; this branch 99p = 220ms (approx 31% improvement) while 50p saw a negligible 2% regression in throughput when dynamic precision was disabled and a 5% improvement when enabled. - KV correctness: synthetic fuzz tests against real models showed no regression in output equality for requests flagged as safe_mode; quarantined requests were validated before reinsertion.

CI and iteration: - Initial CI run failed two unit tests related to deterministic seed ordering in kv_cache_manager; fixed by making reinsertion order deterministic under test mode. - Re-ran CI, all checks passed including linux build, unit tests, integration tests, perf harness smoke. CI timeline: fail -> fix -> pass.

Review conversation (high-level): - Connor Li: asked for explicit invariants on KV reinsertion to ensure we never leak stale kv entries across tenants. Action: added per-tenant namespace enforcement and tests. - Marta Ruiz: requested telemetry for how often dynamic precision flips to enable future cost accounting. Action: added kernel_selector telemetry counters and a console dashboard tile planned in ENG-915. - Devon Patel: suggested a simpler-safe fallback for extremely short sequences to avoid classification overhead. Action: special-case short sequences and added microbenchmarks. - Final approvals from Connor and Marta after fixes.

Rollout plan: - feature flags behind configs.fallback_policy.enable_selective (off by default for enterprise private deployments). - Ramp on hosted: enable 5% traffic -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% while monitoring p99, errors, and kv eviction metrics. - If kv reinsertion rate or mismatches exceed threshold, auto-disable and open rollback alert.

Documentation: design doc included and a short runbook added to docs/ops/fallback_runbook.md describing metrics, alerts, and manual rollback steps.

Notes for on-call: watch eviction_rate, kv_quarantine_size, precision_toggle_rate, and p99 for the top 10 routes. There is an emergency env var REDWOOD_FALLBACK_SAFE_MODE=on to force conservative behavior cluster-wide.

Merge: squash and merge after CI green and approvals. Merge method: squash.
